evidence: Fig. 1.1 caption ends: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] — a schematic of a documented mechanism, not a screenshot or a measurement". Preface, PDF p. 19 (printed p. xv): "ILLUSTRATIVE (Axis 1, provenance) — a non-canonical worked example ([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED)" and "FACT — directly stated by the source." The adjacent Fig. 1.2 caption (PDF p. 35, printed p. 11) uses "[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" for a schematic of the same kind.
issue: Axis-1/Axis-2 label-pair mismatch against the book's own declared vocabulary: ILLUSTRATIVE is declared to pair with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED, and FACT ("directly stated by the source") contradicts the caption's own statement that the drawing is the author's schematic rather than a measurement. As written the tag asserts both a non-canonical provenance and a first-party factual assertion.
fix_instruction: Re-label Fig. 1.1 as [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] (or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]) for the drawing, and, if a FACT claim about the underlying mechanism is intended, give it its own source-cited tag (e.g. "[1P][FACT] for the mechanism; [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] for the schematic").

evidence: "[1P][HYPOTHESIS]: for the canonical 2,000-user workload with ~10 rps average, the incremental per-request compute cost of the 768-dim (all-mpnet) vs 384-dim (MiniLM) embedding models — a cross-model difference, not a dim-only sweep — is ~11.1 GFLOP per 64-token query (2 × params × L: 14.08 − 2.94 GFLOP, the Table 5-1 embedding table's own rows)." Preface, PDF p. 21 (printed p. xvii): "Arithmetic belongs on the epistemic-status axis, not the provenance axis: a worked example computed from a model card is [1P][DERIVED], never [2°]."
issue: The 11.1 GFLOP figure is pure arithmetic on two model-card parameter counts (Table 5-1's own [1P][FACT] rows), so its epistemic status is DERIVED, not HYPOTHESIS ("reasoned but not yet validated"). The sentence also mixes canonical-scenario inputs (2,000 users, 10 rps) into a row whose Axis-1 provenance is declared as first-party.
fix_instruction: Relabel the GFLOP delta as [1P][DERIVED] (and move the canonical-workload framing into a separate [canonical scenario] clause); keep [1P][HYPOTHESIS] only for the genuinely open claim that the ~15% MAP uplift transfers to the target corpus.

evidence: "Suppose user research and demand modeling independently set the busy-period peak to 50 requests/s (a declared scenario input at this growth scale, not a figure derived from the 500-user count...)" and "nhosts = ⌈50 rps × 8.6 s / 17 slots⌉ = ⌈25.29⌉ = 26 hosts (full utilization)" and "then 39 hosts before the spare, 40 under the book's provisioning policy". fix_instruction: Tag the 5,000-employee / 10% / 50 rps inputs [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and the resulting 26 / 38 / 39 / 40 host counts [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED], or state in a single sentence that the whole §4.8 growth variant is [ILLUSTRATIVE].

evidence: Fig. 6.2's own rendered labels include "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)", while the caption states "the 2 s line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Table 4-2 (PDF p. 90, printed p. 66) records "TTFT SLO | 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); p95 ≤ 2 s" and PDF p. 104 (printed p. 80): "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
issue: Figure-label vs. book-terminology contradiction: the in-figure annotation labels 2 s as the "TTFT budget", which is exactly the conflation the chapter text and Table 4-2 forbid (budget = 1.2 s; ceiling = 2 s). A reader who takes the figure as the SLO definition will plan against the wrong number and will also mis-apply the "p95 ≤ 2 s" ceiling to TTFT only.
fix_instruction: Relabel the Fig. 6.2 line as "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (and, if the 1.2 s design budget is drawn, label it separately), so the rendered figure matches the caption and Table 4-2.

evidence: Body text: "The figure shows one group's geometry: 8 query heads funnel into a single shared K/V head." The rendered figure (attached image of printed p. 135) draws three groups of eight query heads funnelling into three K/V boxes and carries the label "8 q : 1 KV per group (8 total; 3 shown)".
issue: The prose misdescribes what the figure shows: the drawing is explicitly three of the eight groups (per the figure's own label), not "one group's geometry". The caption's "The head glyphs are schematic" does not license the body text's misreading, and a reader checking the 8:1 ratio against the picture sees three K/V boxes rather than one.
fix_instruction: Change the sentence to "The figure shows three of the eight groups (8 query heads funnelling into one shared K/V head each)", matching the figure's own "8 total; 3 shown" label.

evidence: "The short version, each mechanism bound to the one constraint it attacks: the KV cache itself is the capacity demand (it is the state, and its size per sequence is what must fit); PagedAttention → fragmentation (it manages where that state lives on the device and wastes less of it); prefix caching → redundant compute (it avoids computing a shared prefix's K/V twice); quantization → bytes per element (it shrinks each element); offloading → residency (it moves some of that state elsewhere)."
issue: Ambiguous pronoun in a definition list: in three of the five parentheticals "it" can grammatically attach to the constraint on the left of the arrow, giving false readings ("redundant compute avoids computing...", "bytes per element shrinks each element", "residency moves some of that state elsewhere"). The list is the book's compact mechanism→constraint map and is reused in later chapters, so the referent must be unambiguous.
fix_instruction: Replace "it" with the mechanism name in each parenthetical (e.g. "prefix caching avoids computing a shared prefix's K/V twice"), keeping one subject per definition.
